info.name: Fashion Express API
info.description:
Fashion Express backend.

**Run `Auth -> Sign in` first.** Authentication is a session cookie, not a bearer token; Postman's cookie jar replays it automatically.

Select the *Fashion Express (local)* environment top-right and set `username` / `password` to a real account. There are no default logins — see api/users.md for creating the first one.

**Why the collection sets an `Origin` header on every request:** once you hold a session cookie, better-auth refuses its own routes unless the request declares a trusted origin (403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN). A collection-level pre-request script adds it from {{origin}}, which must appear in the server's TRUSTED_ORIGINS.

Money and IDs are strings, never JSON numbers (NFR-01).

exec: // better-auth refuses its routes when a session cookie is present and no
// trusted Origin is declared (403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN). Postman does
// not send Origin on its own, so set it here for every request.

request.description: The one route needing no session. `migrations` should match the number of files in src/database/migrations.

Run this first. Postman stores the session cookie and replays it on every later request — there is no bearer token to copy.

Saves the signed-in account's id to {{currentUserId}} so the Users requests can avoid editing you by accident.
The caller's user type and full permission list. The quickest way to see why a request was refused.
better-auth's own view. /me is what an application should use.

Requires the current password.

NOTE: this really does change it. Update the environment's `password` afterwards or the next Sign in will fail.
Clears the cookie. Everything after this returns 401 until you sign in again.
All twelve lists with their capabilities. Use `create`, `delete` and `editableFields` to decide which buttons to draw (FR-12.5.2).
Paginated at 25 (RD-12). Returns active AND inactive entries — the admin screen needs to see what it retired.

Active entries only — what a dropdown should use.

Scoped lists (statuses, payment-methods) REQUIRE ?scope=, or you get a 400. Enable the scope param for those.
What breaks if this entry is retired. Ask before offering Delete.

Permission: manage_referencedata.

Coded lists take code+label; named lists (job-positions, departments, categories) take `name`; statuses and payment-methods also require `scope`.

Structural lists refuse this with a 400.

Saves the new id to {{refId}}.

Permission: manage_referencedata.

`code` and `scope` are absent from the DTO — sending either is a 400. A code is fixed once created (BR-59).

On a structural list only `label` is accepted; even isActive is refused.
The supported way to retire an entry (BR-60). It leaves every picker while existing records keep their meaning.

Permission: manage_referencedata. 204 on success.

409 if anything uses it — deactivate instead. 400 on a structural list, where deletion is not a thing at all.
Permission: view_user. Page size is fixed at 10 (RD-12).
Permission: view_user.

Permission: add_user. The account and its credential are written in one transaction, so the new user can sign in immediately.

`employeeId` is generated and rejected if sent (FR-00.8). `salary` must be a decimal STRING.

Saves the new id to {{userId}} so the requests below act on it.

request.description:
Permission: change_user. Send only what changes.

`username`, `employeeId`, `isSuperuser` and `isManager` are all refused with 400 — privilege comes from userTypeId.

CAREFUL: setting {"statusCode":"inactive"} or "on_leave" on your OWN account ends your session immediately, because only an active account may authenticate. Point {{userId}} at someone else before trying it.
Permission: change_user, except anyone may change their own. Returns 204.

Permission: delete_user AND a superuser type.

Rarely right: anyone who has submitted a bill claim cannot be deleted (409). Deactivate with Update instead.
Permission: view_user.
Permission: manage_referencedata.
Permission: view_shop. Each row counts the customers, products, sales and staff it holds (FR-11.2.2) — check these before deactivating.
Active shops. No permission needed: every create form must choose a shop (BR-49).
Permission: add_shop. BR-47: the name is unique ignoring case.
Permission: change_shop.
FR-11.2.3 — the normal way to retire a shop. It leaves the pickers but keeps its history and still appears in reports.

Permission: delete_shop.

BR-48: refused with a 409 if the shop holds any customer, product, sale or staff account. Deletion is only for a shop created in error and never used.
Permission: view_customer. Search covers name, customer ID, company and phone (FR-03.3).
The customer picker for a sale. shopId is REQUIRED — a sale's customer must belong to the sale's shop (BR-53).
FR-03.6.1 — call before offering Delete. Deleting a customer cascades to every sale, payment and allocation they own (BR-21).

Permission: add_customer.

The customer number is generated (FE26082026-01) and rejected if sent. The serial is continuous — it does not restart daily (BR-46).

Permission: change_customer.

`customerId` and `shopId` are both refused with 400: the number is immutable (FR-03.2) and BR-54 fixes the shop at creation.
Permission: delete_customer. Irreversible and cascading — show Deletion impact first.

Permission: view_inventoryitem.

The `summary` block describes the current FILTER, not the current page (FR-04.4).
The line-item picker for a sale. shopId is REQUIRED: a sale may only draw on its own shop's stock (BR-50).
BR-24: quantity at or below the item's own minimum. Evaluated per shop (BR-52).

FR-04.5, paginated at 20. READ ONLY — BR-25: movements are written only by the system and never edited or deleted.

`quantity` is absolute; the sign comes from the type's `direction`.

Permission: add_inventoryitem.

`partCode` is unique WITHIN THE SHOP (BR-51) — two shops may each stock CLP-001.

Creating with stock writes an opening Stock In movement.

Permission: change_inventoryitem.

Raising the quantity records a Stock In (`Stock added via edit`); lowering it records an Adjustment (`Stock adjusted via edit`). Units and boxes are logged separately (BR-26).

`shopId` is refused: BR-54 fixes it at creation.

Permission: delete_inventoryitem.

BR-27: refused with a 409 if the product appears on any sale line.
Permission: view_supplier. Search matches name or phone. Totals purchased/paid/due per supplier (FR-05.2, FR-05.4).
For the inventory form's supplier reference (FR-04.1.1).
Permission: add_supplier. Suppliers are NOT shop-scoped (FR-11.4).
`due` is derived from price minus payments and never entered (BR-28).

Permission: add_supplier.

Add `initialPayment` + `initialPaymentMethodId` to pay at the same time — BR-32 saves both atomically, and refuses an initial payment above the price.

Permission: add_supplierpayment.

Three rules reject a payment:
- BR-29: a reference number is required for LC, cheque, TT and bank; cash needs none.
- BR-62: the method must be supplier-scoped — get it from Reference data -> Picker options with ?scope=supplier.
- BR-30: it may not exceed the purchase's remaining due.

Posts a Debit to the ledger automatically (BR-38).

Permission: add_supplierpayment.

BR-31: allocated OLDEST PURCHASE FIRST by purchase date, and may not exceed the supplier's total outstanding. Each purchase touched gets its own payment row, receipt number and ledger entry.

request.description: BR-40 — the ledger entry is updated to match.
BR-40 — the ledger entry is removed with it.

Permission: view_sale.

BR-01: a non-manager sees ONLY the sales they created. `totals` respects every filter; with itemType set they are apportioned by line share (BR-15).
A sale the caller may not see returns 404, not 403 — learning it exists would already break BR-01.

Permission: add_sale.

A stocked line with no unitPrice takes the product's current price; a positive price always wins.

BR-04: a machine line needs a description, a stocked line needs a product. BR-50/BR-53: the product and customer must be in the sale's shop.

Add `initialPayment` to take money on the same form.
Quotation mode (FR-02.2). A quotation cannot take a payment (BR-11).
FR-02.3.1 — becomes a draft invoice, keeping items and prices.

Permission: finalize_sale — its OWN permission (FR-02.4.3).

IRREVERSIBLE. Validates every line before deducting any (BR-06), deducts stock, writes a movement per product naming the sale, and starts the sale counting toward revenue.

`nowLowOnStock` lists items that have just fallen to or below their minimum (FR-02.4.2).

Permission: add_salepayment. Posts a Credit to the ledger (BR-38).

BR-09 total may not exceed the sale value; BR-10 no zero; BR-11 not on a cancelled sale or quotation; BR-62 the method must be customer-scoped.
On a FINALISED sale this is administrators-only (FR-02.6.1) and deducts stock immediately (BR-13).

On a FINALISED sale: administrators-only, and BR-12 returns the stock with a reversing movement.

FR-02.6.2: if this empties the sale it reverts to draft and its payments are deleted — the response says how many.
BR-14 — only DRAFT sales may be deleted.
FR-03.4 — every finalised order with totals across the whole relationship, plus the payment events and how many invoices each was spread across.
FR-03.5.1 — offer the payment action only when this is above zero.

Permission: add_customerpayment.

BR-16: applied OLDEST FINALISED SALE FIRST until exhausted. BR-17: may not exceed the customer's total outstanding — if it would, the whole event is rejected and nothing is written. BR-18: each sale touched gets its own real payment row and receipt. BR-19: grouped under one reference.
BR-19 — every invoice the event settled and the amount applied to each.

Permission: view_expense.

`filteredTotal` is the total of everything matching the filter; `ledgerBalance` is business-wide and deliberately unfiltered (FR-06.5).

FR-06.4 precedence: an explicit from/to beats a single date, which beats month.
FR-09.1 — ranked by size. Grouped by category id; renaming a category never re-buckets history.
FR-06.6 — if it came from an approved claim, `claim` carries who submitted and who approved it.

Permission: add_expense ONLY — BR-33 lets anyone with it create one, including a non-manager.

Posts a Debit to the ledger (BR-38). `shopId` is optional; null means a business-wide cost (§10.2).
BR-33 — MANAGERS ONLY, even for the person who created it. The ledger entry moves with the amount (BR-40).
BR-33 — managers only. Removes the ledger entry too (BR-40).

Scope follows your permissions, not the URL: `view_my_bills` sees your own (FR-07.3), `review_bills` sees everyone's (FR-07.4).

`totals` carries the pending/approved/rejected figures together.
Permission: submit_bill. Starts `pending` — the status is set by the workflow and is never sent (FR-07.1.1).

FR-07.2 — pick a file for `attachment` in the Body tab.

BR-34 whitelist: pdf jpg jpeg png gif bmp webp doc docx xls xlsx csv txt. Anything else is a 400.

The stored name is generated, never the uploaded one, and files live outside the app path (NFR-11).

Permission: review_bills.

BR-36 — ONE action: marks it approved, records who and when, creates an expense dated to the BILL date with the employee as payee, and links the two. All of it or none of it.

Permission: review_bills.

BR-37 — records the reviewer and date and creates NO expense.
Only your own, and only while still pending. BR-35: a reviewed claim cannot be edited, withdrawn or processed again.

Manager-only (FR-09.5) and READ-ONLY — BR-38: no user posts a line by hand.

`totals` is the whole ledger; `filtered` is what you asked for. Render signs from `direction`, never by comparing entry_type to 'credit' (FR-12.12.2).
FR-08.3 — reports what it WOULD post and writes nothing. This is the default if `preview` is omitted.

Actually writes. Safe to run repeatedly: every post is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on (source_id, reference), so a rebuild reconciles and cannot duplicate (BR-39).

`orphaned` lists ledger lines whose underlying record is gone — a rebuild only adds, so it cannot repair those.

FR-01. No permission gate: what you see follows YOUR permissions.

`?shopId=` filters every figure EXCEPT expenses and bill claims, which are not shop-scoped and sit in `businessWide` with a note saying so (FR-01.8).

`topProducts` covers stocked AND machine lines; machine lines group by the first meaningful line of their description (FR-01.4).

A bills-only user gets `reduced: true` and just two actions (FR-01.7) — check that flag before rendering anything else.
FR-01.6 — the count that must appear on EVERY page. Cheap enough to call from a layout.

Manager-only (FR-09.5). The ledger balance (FR-09.2) and the per-shop breakdown (FR-09.6).

No per-shop net profit: expenses are largely business-wide, so dividing them would be arbitrary.

FR-09.3 — five sheets: Employees, Customers, Inventory, Expenses, Payments. Money is written as numbers with a format, so totals actually sum.

In Postman use Send > 'Send and Download'.
FR-09.4 — every customer with invoiced/paid/due and a grand-total row built from real SUM formulas.

FR-02.9. A quotation prints on its OWN template: titled QUOTATION, stating it is not an invoice, valid 30 days, and with no balance lines.

BR-01 applies — an employee gets 404 for someone else's sale.
Scoped by BR-01 like every other read.
Landscape, with totals over FINALISED sales only (BR-03) even though drafts are listed.
Readable by anyone — the letterhead is needed to render documents.
Manager-only. FR-10.1 — appears on every printed invoice and receipt from now on.

request.description: FR-10.2 — the four groups with their permission and account counts.
Superuser only. Reports whether the tool is enabled and the exact phrases it demands.

FR-10.3. WITHOUT `confirmation` this previews and writes nothing (BR-43).

Some targets cannot be cleared alone — clearing expenses without billClaims would leave an approved claim with no expense, which the database refuses. The tool says so up front rather than failing halfway, and never widens your selection for you.

*** THIS DELETES DATA IRREVERSIBLY ***

Four safeguards: BR-41 superuser only; BR-42 needs ENABLE_DATA_CLEANUP=true; BR-43 this exact phrase; BR-44 administrators and your own account are preserved unless you also send includeAdminsConfirmation with the SECOND, different phrase.
